A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, core methodology, and principal experiments. The text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and Appendices A–C report original Gaussian simulations, image-deblurring model-selection experiments, and MRI selection and OOD-detection results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds a Gaussian optimizer-discrepancy analysis, Poisson-noise experiments, and a DINOv2-based MRI result.

M1.justification: The core cross-validation framework and scoring rules remain unchanged. Appendix C.2 adds an operational Poisson adaptation using binomial data fission and Prox-DiffPIR with PIDAL/ADMM for positivity-constrained posterior guidance. This extends the procedure for the new noise scenario.

E1.justification: v2 adds Poisson-noise deblurring at blur strength 0.5 using the existing natural-image populations. This introduces a distinct measurement-noise scenario beyond v1's Gaussian experiments; the image datasets, MRI populations, and principal tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the Bayesian residual and empirical Bayesian residual baselines. The FFHQ/AFHQ and brain/knee candidate priors also remain unchanged. PIDAL and Prox-DiffPIR support the new implementation, while DINOv2 supplies an internal scoring variant rather than a new external selection baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds a Poisson protocol with gamma = 0.05, an MRI scoring check using DINOv2 embeddings, and an alpha-dependent comparison of parameter optima. Section 4.3.1 also corrects the listed mild blur from 0.05 to 0.5, consistent with v1's Table 2 and figure captions; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Figure 13 examines discrepancies between split-data and marginal-likelihood parameter optima across alpha and dimension. Appendix C.3 adds a brief embedding-sensitivity check using DINOv2. Existing blur/alpha sensitivity, Monte Carlo convergence, and failure-case analyses are retained despite relocation.

E5.justification: v1 already documents averaging over 25 noise realizations for Figures 11–12; v2 makes this explicit in their displays and uses the same practice for Figure 13. The 95th-percentile OOD test is retained, with no new seed-reporting, confidence-interval, or uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Existing tabulated results are unchanged, including v1 Table 8, now v2 Table 9. New Poisson Table 8 reports 6.7% Type I error for both ID subsets, 80% power for moderate OOD, and 100% for strong OOD. v2 also adds Figure 13's optimizer-discrepancy results and reports 100% brain-image accuracy with DINOv2, without an acceleration-specific breakdown.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds the formal Poisson observation model, binomial splitting construction, and conditional distributions in Equations 20–23. The Gaussian derivation remains unchanged. New Equation 23 omits the blur operator A from its rates despite Equation 20 using A(x), leaving an internal formula inconsistency.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of unsupervised selection and misspecification testing from a single measurement, compatibility with modern Bayesian imaging samplers, and computationally efficient discrimination. The added experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the Poisson results as maintaining similar detection performance with noisier measurements. It uses the DINOv2 result to emphasize embedding suitability and suggests embedding aggregation. Appendix A adds discussion of vanishing optimizer discrepancy as alpha decreases; earlier hallucination and MRI limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.3.1 newly specifies Gaussian noise sigma = 0.05. Appendix C.2 documents reused networks, a 1000-iteration PIDAL limit, relative stopping tolerance of 10^-4, mu = 20, and 300 Prox-DiffPIR iterations per sample. Existing hardware disclosures and code/data access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for PIDAL, low-photon Bayesian computation, Prox-DiffPIR, and DINOv2. These support the appendix extensions. The broader related-work discussion and positioning against existing selection and OOD approaches remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes local grammatical corrections, repairs supplementary-section references, modestly reorders Appendix C.1 discussion, and inserts the Poisson subsection before MRI. It also expands the acknowledgements. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 13 and 19 and Poisson Table 8, while relocating and resizing retained displays. For example, v1 Figure 7 becomes v2 Figure 6, and the MRI table becomes Table 9. Figures 11–12 explicitly label noise averaging. The overall visual format is preserved.

improvement.justification: Appendix C.2 gives empirical and implementation support for non-Gaussian applicability that v1 only stated, while Figure 13 directly examines the parameter-selection consequences of splitting. The added settings also improve reproducibility. These are useful, limited gains, tempered by the inconsistent Poisson rates in Equation 23 and the sparse specification of the DINOv2 result.
